data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A panel of non-experts using a checklist will be more reliable than a single expert because the checklist decomposes complex intuition into a series of independent binary verifications, eliminating single-point cognitive failure.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The checklist is poorly designed and omits critical variables that the expert's intuition would have captured.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The panel exhibits 'groupthink' or social contagion, leading them to collectively ignore a checklist item.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The task requires holistic synthesis that cannot be decomposed into a checklist without losing essential context.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The 'Error-Cancellation Mechanism': While a single expert's intuition is a monolithic heuristic susceptible to 'blind spots' or confirmation bias, a checklist forces the decomposition of the problem into discrete, verifiable sub-tasks. By distributing these tasks across a panel, the probability of a systemic oversight is reduced to the joint probability of all panel members missing the same specific checklist item, which is significantly lower than the probability of a single expert's intuition failing.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
